story: Ask HN: What’s the most important modern simple invention?
text: I'm surprised nobody mentioned radio communication. The AM (Amplitude Modulation) transmission is even quite simple to understand and build. You can even create an electric arc between the ground and the transmitting tower as a cheap (and dangerous) receiver: [VIDEO]

I'm not entirely sure what process is converting to sound, but the metal fence makes a great antenna and we are talking about 10's of feet from the antenna with 500 kW AM at 200 kHz going into it. It could actually have been arcing: [VIDEO]
Also you can hear AM radio transmission if you short the tower: [VIDEO] Electricity is both awesome and terrifying

story: Radio frequency hearing in humans and its effects (2003)
text: I grew up in a house that was next door to a radio rebroadcasting facility, and we could definitely hear the radio station coming from the walls of our house sometimes, e.g. even their station identification so there was no ambiguity. I assumed it was the house wiring (mostly knob and tube) acting as an antenna. I'm reasonably sure that was AM, though. Was the sound you heard like either of these? [VIDEO] [LINK]
